gate_reasoning: Stage 3 scores 69 Low out of 93 total claims (74.2% Low), exceeding the 70% FAIL threshold. The dominant failure modes are: (1) 21 explicitly tagged [ASSUMED-N] claims with zero source backing, concentrated in the most commercially sensitive cost figures across all four pain points; (2) 16 company-profile claims sourced solely from company self-descriptions with no independent corroboration; (3) all market-sizing claims are either single secondary-market-research sources, APAC-aggregate proxies, or bottom-up estimates with no primary-gov cross-validation; (4) the LD rate arithmetic that underpins the quantified cost case for PP3.1 and PP3.2 rests entirely on personal legal blogs. Only 2 claims reach High confidence (the regulatory framework on site-inspection requirements, and the regulatory tightening evidence for emissions standards), both of which are regulatory-text claims rather than market or cost claims. The stage contains strong structural narrative and well-organized hypothesis frameworks, but the quantitative cost and frequency claims required to make pain points investable are almost uniformly unsupported. Deep research must prioritize: (a) primary-gov or primary-association validation of the 7.4% Indonesia construction certification rate, and (b) primary-source grounding for the 0.5%/week EPC LD rate that drives all cost quantification.
